_comment: BUG-002, new standard mechanism (2026-10-07): tests Core1Runner's fixed_schedule (deadline-anchored) pacing, verified against Betaflight's own source as the architecturally correct fix for the retuning fragility that core1_interval_us's sleep-after-work pad kept hitting (see BUG-002.md's 'Telemetry overhead'/Betaflight-comparison sections - Betaflight's scheduler.c: nextTargetCycles = lastTargetCycles + desiredPeriodCycles, immune to per-call cost as long as cost < period). core1_interval_us=1045 here is the ABSOLUTE PERIOD TARGET, not a pad - this is the same ~1042-1048us average that gave pad-140 its original 94-97% KPI (bug-reports/BUG-002-...md's dose-response work), chosen so this test is a mechanism comparison (deadline vs. sleep-after-work) at a matched target, not a new tuning search. Unlike every *_padded_*.json file, this should not need re-tuning if update()'s own cost changes again - that is exactly the property being tested. Run interleaved and rotated against bins_off (natural/unpaced) and padded_276 (the sleep-after-work re-tune), not in a block, to compare all three mechanisms at once.
